chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said:

I said to him: A man upon whom was the obligation of the Hajj of Islam, so he intended to perform Hajj. It was said to him: 'Marry, then perform Hajj.' So he said: 'If I marry before I perform Hajj, then my slave is free.' So he married before he performed Hajj. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His slave should be freed.' I said: 'He did not intend the Face of Allah by freeing him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is a vow in obedience to Allah, and Hajj is more rightful than marriage, and more obligatory upon him than marriage.' I said: 'Suppose Hajj is optional (voluntary)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Even if it is voluntary, it is an obedience to Allah, and he has freed his slave.'
ai.seo_question: Does a vow to free a slave based on marrying before Hajj remain valid if the person performs Hajj first?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the vow to free a slave upon marrying before Hajj remains valid even if the man performs the optional Hajj first, as the condition was fulfilled by the act of marriage itself. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that a vow (nadhr) constitutes an act of obedience (ta'ah) to Allah, thereby validating the emancipation regardless of whether the primary act (Hajj) was performed in its optimal order. The Imam further establishes that Hajj holds greater religious priority than marriage, reinforcing the hierarchy of obligations in personal status matters.
